Following Apple's extension of the testing cycle for macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, the company is now rolling out the seventh Release Candidate (RC) for both operating systems. Here are the details.

New Release Candidates Released

Four days ago, Apple released the sixth Release Candidate for macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, while also issuing the first Release Candidate for macOS 26.6 and its related versions.

Judging by the timing and the number of release candidates, it would be natural to assume these were the final rounds of testing before the official rollout. Turns out that's not the case.

Today, Apple released the seventh Release Candidate for macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.8, with the following build numbers:

  • macOS Sonoma 14.8.8 (23J620)
  • macOS Sequoia 15.7.8 (24G824)

Both builds are now available for download by developers and public beta testers.

Apple has yet to disclose the specific update contents for the two systems, only stating the usual line: "This update provides important security fixes and is recommended for all users to install." The company will most likely publish further details on the Apple security updates page after the two systems are officially released.

Apple has consistently been issuing updates for older versions of its operating systems, bringing important bug fixes to users who are unable to upgrade to the latest software. This instance is likely a similar case, so users still running macOS Sonoma or Sequoia should install the update as soon as it is officially released, which is expected to be no earlier than early next week.
